intro: The control pilot (CP) is one wire in every charging cable. The charger puts a voltage on it, and the car pulls that voltage down with resistors. From the level, both sides know whether a car is connected and whether it wants power. A 1 kHz square wave on the same wire tells the car how much current it may take.

plug.title: Plug in
plug.text: Before the plug goes in, the charger holds CP at +12 V: state A. The car's resistor pulls it down to +9 V: state B. The charger also reads the cable's rating from the PP pin.

offer.title: Offer current
offer.text: The charger starts a 1 kHz square wave on CP. The share of time it is high, the duty cycle, is the current the car may take. The house allows 24 A, so the 32 A charger offers 24 A: 40 %.

charge.title: Charge
charge.text: The car switches in a second resistor: CP drops to +6 V, state C. Only now does the charger close its contactor. The car takes up to 24 A on each phase.

reduce.title: Less current
reduce.text: The house needs its power elsewhere. Its energy manager tells the charger, and the charger lowers the duty cycle to 10 %: 6 A. The car has 5 s to follow.

stop.title: Stop
stop.text: The battery is full. The car opens its switch: CP goes back to +9 V, state B. The charger opens the contactor.

unplug.title: Unplug
unplug.text: The plug comes out. CP returns to +12 V, state A, and the charger stops the square wave.

frames.pp: This cable carries up to 32 A

notes.b1: The charger feeds +12 V through a 1 kΩ resistor. The car connects 2.74 kΩ from CP to protective earth (PE), behind a diode, and the voltage drops to +9 V. B1 means state B with a steady voltage; B2 is the same state with the square wave.
notes.pp: Proximity pilot (PP) is not a signal. It is a resistor in the cable's plug, between PP and PE, and its value is the cable's rating: 1.5 kΩ is 13 A, 680 Ω is 20 A, 220 Ω is 32 A, 100 Ω is 63 A.
notes.pwm: One period lasts 1 ms. CP is at +9 V for 40 % of it (0.4 ms) and at −12 V for the rest. Between 10 % and 85 %, the current is the duty cycle × 0.6 A: 40 × 0.6 = 24 A.
notes.c: The car closes its switch S2 and adds 1.3 kΩ beside the 2.74 kΩ. The high level of the square wave drops to +6 V. With 270 Ω instead, it would drop to +3 V: state D, which asks for ventilation.
notes.contactor: Not a signal on CP. The charger's contactor connects L1, L2, L3 and N to the car, and the car's on-board charger turns the AC into DC for the battery.
notes.limit: Not IEC 61851: an energy manager speaks Modbus, OCPP or closes a contact. The car never sees this message, only the new duty cycle.
notes.pwm-10: 10 × 0.6 = 6 A, the lowest current a duty cycle can offer. The car must lower its current within 5 s.
notes.b2: The car opens S2 and the high level goes back to +9 V. A good car lowers its current first, so that the contactor does not open under load.
notes.open: In state B the charger must not supply power, so it opens the contactor. The square wave goes on: the car could ask for power again.
notes.a: Nothing pulls CP down any more: +12 V, state A. The charger stops the square wave (A1) and waits for the next car.

facts.between: Charger (EVSE) ↔ car, on every Type 1, Type 2 and CCS plug
facts.transport: One wire, CP, against protective earth: ±12 V and a 1 kHz square wave
facts.security: None. It is an analog signal inside the cable.
facts.frames: States A +12 V · B +9 V · C +6 V · D +3 V · E 0 V · F −12 V
facts.speed: 1 kHz. The car follows a new duty cycle within 5 s.

tips: Check the low level too. A square wave that does not reach −12 V means the car's diode is missing or shorted, and the charger must not switch on.
5 % is not a current. It means "talk digitally first" (ISO 15118): the limit then comes from the messages, not from the duty cycle.
The cable limits the current too. With a 20 A cable (680 Ω), a 32 A charger offers at most 20 A: a duty cycle of 33.3 %.
State D (+3 V) asks for ventilation. A charger without a fan for the room must not charge in state D. E (0 V) is a short or no power; F (−12 V) means the charger is not available.

timing.title: The control pilot, 3 ms of each state
timing.note: Each line is the CP voltage: −12 V at the bottom, +12 V at the top (level = (V + 12) / 24). The square wave repeats every 1 ms. Its duty cycle is the current: 40 % is 24 A, 10 % is 6 A. Above 85 %, the current is (duty − 64) × 2.5 A, up to 80 A at 96 %. 5 % asks for digital communication. The low level stays at −12 V in every state: the diode in the car lets no current through in that direction.
